name: Vanilla Bedrock
author: nicholas@skynode.pro
description:
Bedrock Edition (also known as the Bedrock Version, Bedrock Codebase, Bedrock Engine or just Bedrock) refers to the multi-platform family of editions of Minecraft developed by Mojang AB, Microsoft Studios, 4J Studios, and SkyBox Labs. Prior to this term, as the engine originated with Pocket Edition, this entire product family was referred to as "Pocket Edition", "MCPE", or "Pocket/Windows 10 Edition".

Skynode build: configures the NetherNet transport (server-udp-ports with the public allocation IP) on every boot so Bedrock 26.51+ clients can join through Pterodactyl. Repo: https://github.com/skynodehost/eggs

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash

apt update
apt install -y zip unzip wget curl

if [ ! -d /mnt/server/ ]; then
    mkdir /mnt/server/
fi

cd /mnt/server

# Minecraft CDN Akamai blocks script user-agents
RANDVERSION=$(echo $((1 + $RANDOM % 4000)))

if [ -z "${BEDROCK_VERSION}" ] || [ "${BEDROCK_VERSION}" == "latest" ]; then
    echo -e "\n Downloading latest Bedrock server"
    DOWNLOAD_URL=$(curl -A "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/90.0.$RANDVERSION.212 Safari/537.36" -H "Accept-Language: en" -H "Accept-Encoding: json" -H "content-type: application/json" https://net-secondary.web.minecraft-services.net/api/v1.0/download/links | grep -o 'https://www.minecraft.net/bedrockdedicatedserver/bin-linux/[^"]*')
else 
    echo -e "\n Downloading ${BEDROCK_VERSION} Bedrock server"
    DOWNLOAD_URL=https://www.minecraft.net/bedrockdedicatedserver/bin-linux/bedrock-server-$BEDROCK_VERSION.zip
fi

DOWNLOAD_FILE=$(echo ${DOWNLOAD_URL} | cut -d"/" -f5) # Retrieve archive name

echo -e "backing up config files"
rm *.bak versions.html.gz
cp server.properties server.properties.bak
cp permissions.json permissions.json.bak
cp allowlist.json allowlist.json.bak


echo -e "Downloading files from: $DOWNLOAD_URL"

curl -L -A "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/90.0.$RANDVERSION.212 Safari/537.36" -H "Accept-Language: en" -o $DOWNLOAD_FILE $DOWNLOAD_URL

echo -e "Unpacking server files"
unzip -o $DOWNLOAD_FILE

echo -e "Cleaning up after installing"
rm $DOWNLOAD_FILE

echo -e "restoring backup config files - on first install there will be file not found errors which you can ignore."
cp -rf server.properties.bak server.properties
cp -rf permissions.json.bak permissions.json
cp -rf allowlist.json.bak allowlist.json

chmod +x bedrock_server

echo -e "Writing NetherNet start wrapper"
cat > start.sh <<'START_EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Skynode Vanilla Bedrock start wrapper.
#
# Bedrock Dedicated Server 26.51+ only accepts the NetherNet transport. Clients do
# HTTP signaling over TCP on server-port, then play over the UDP ports listed in
# server-udp-ports. The server advertises that list to clients, so behind the
# Pterodactyl Docker bridge it must carry the public allocation IP, not the
# container IP. This script rewrites server-udp-ports from the allocation on
# every boot and then starts bedrock_server.
set -u
cd /home/container || exit 1
PROPS=server.properties

if [ ! -f "$PROPS" ]; then
  echo "[nethernet] $PROPS not found, starting with server defaults"
  exec ./bedrock_server
fi

prop() { grep -E "^$1=" "$PROPS" | tail -n1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '\r'; }

TRANSPORT="$(prop transport)"
if [ -z "$TRANSPORT" ]; then
  # Worlds created before Bedrock 26.50 have no transport line and would fall back to RakNet.
  TRANSPORT=nethernet
  printf 'transport=nethernet\n' >> "$PROPS"
fi
PORT="${SERVER_PORT:-$(prop server-port)}"
PUBLIC_IP="${NETHERNET_PUBLIC_IP:-${SERVER_IP:-}}"
UDP_PORTS="$(printf '%s' "${UDP_PORTS:-}" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
[ -z "$UDP_PORTS" ] && UDP_PORTS="$PORT"

if [ "$TRANSPORT" != "nethernet" ]; then
  echo "[nethernet] WARNING: transport=$TRANSPORT. Current Bedrock clients only connect over NetherNet."
  exec ./bedrock_server
fi

entries=""
count=0
IFS=',' read -ra ranges <<< "$UDP_PORTS"
for range in "${ranges[@]}"; do
  if [[ "$range" =~ ^([0-9]+)(-([0-9]+))?$ ]]; then
    first="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    last="${BASH_REMATCH[3]:-$first}"
    if [ "$last" -lt "$first" ]; then
      echo "[nethernet] WARNING: ignoring reversed UDP range '$range'"
      continue
    fi
    count=$((count + last - first + 1))
    if [ -n "$PUBLIC_IP" ]; then
      entry="$PUBLIC_IP:$range:$range"
    else
      entry="$range"
    fi
    entries="${entries:+$entries,}$entry"
  else
    echo "[nethernet] WARNING: ignoring invalid UDP port entry '$range'"
  fi
done

if [ -z "$entries" ]; then
  echo "[nethernet] WARNING: no usable UDP ports configured, leaving server-udp-ports unchanged"
  exec ./bedrock_server
fi

# server-udp-ports accumulates across duplicate lines, so keep exactly one.
sed -i '/^server-udp-ports=/d' "$PROPS"
printf 'server-udp-ports=%s\n' "$entries" >> "$PROPS"

echo "[nethernet] Signaling: TCP $PORT. Gameplay: UDP $entries ($count port(s))."
if [ -z "$PUBLIC_IP" ]; then
  echo "[nethernet] WARNING: no public IP available. Players outside this node may fail to join."
fi
MAX_PLAYERS="$(prop max-players)"
if [ -n "$MAX_PLAYERS" ] && [ "$count" -lt "$MAX_PLAYERS" ] 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "[nethernet] NOTE: max-players is $MAX_PLAYERS but only $count UDP port(s) are advertised."
  echo "[nethernet]       NetherNet uses one UDP port per connected player. Assign more allocations"
  echo "[nethernet]       to this server and list them in the 'NetherNet UDP Ports' startup variable."
fi

exec ./bedrock_server
START_EOF
chmod +x start.sh

echo -e "Install Completed"

variables.name: Bedrock Version
variables.description:
The version of bedrock. (Ex. 1.7.0.13)

Default version is latest.

variables.name: Allow cheats
variables.description:
If true then cheats like commands can be used.

Allowed values: "true" or "false"

variables.name: Transport
variables.description: Network transport. Bedrock 26.51+ clients only connect over nethernet. raknet is kept only as an emergency switch and no longer works with current clients.

variables.name: NetherNet UDP Ports
variables.description: UDP ports used for gameplay, one per connected player. Comma separated ports or ranges, e.g. 19140-19149. Every port listed must be an allocation assigned to this server. Leave empty to use the primary allocation port only (one player at a time).

variables.name: Public IP Override
variables.description: Public IP advertised to players for NetherNet gameplay. Leave empty to use the primary allocation IP.
